findings.found: the Publisher "CN=Brindlecote Software, O=Brindlecote Ltd, L=Leeds, C=GB" is not the certificate subject "CN=Brindlecote Software Ltd, O=Brindlecote Ltd, L=Leeds, C=GB": the CN is "Brindlecote Software" in the manifest and "Brindlecote Software Ltd" in the certificate subject; signing with that certificate fails
findings.fix: set Publisher to the exact subject of the certificate that signs the package, or sign with the certificate whose subject the manifest names

basis.text: the Publisher must match the publisher subject of the certificate the package is signed with
the Subject of the signing certificate must match the Publisher of the manifest, a distinguished name such as CN=..., O=..., C=...
basis.source: Create a certificate for package signing (MSIX, Microsoft Learn)

basis.text: every MSIX package must be signed before it is installed, and Windows reads the manifest to deploy, show and update the app

findings.own: only with --cert-subject: Identity Publisher against the subject given, compared as text, exactly; the message says which part differs, or that only the spacing or the order differs, because signing fails either way

findings.found: the Version "4.2.70000.0" is not four 16-bit numbers: 70000 is above 65535, the largest 16-bit part
findings.fix: write the version as four numbers from 0 to 65535, such as 1.4.2.0; a build number of a pipeline above 65535 does not fit

basis.text: Name, Publisher and Version are required; Version is in quad notation, major.minor.build.revision; ProcessorArchitecture is x86, x64, arm, arm64, x86a64 or neutral, and a package with executable code has it

findings.own: Identity Version that is not four whole numbers separated by dots, each from 0 to 65535 with no leading zero; the version of a .NET or C++ project often has three parts, or a build number above 65535

findings.found: the MinVersion 10.0.22631.0 of Windows.Desktop is above its MaxVersionTested 10.0.19045.0: the app would install only on builds it was never tested on
findings.fix: write both versions as 10.0.build.0, with MinVersion at or below MaxVersionTested

basis.text: TargetDeviceFamily needs Name, MinVersion and MaxVersionTested, and both versions are in quad notation
basis.source: TargetDeviceFamily in Dependencies (manifest schema, Microsoft Learn)

basis.text: the app is not applicable on a system older than MinVersion, and MaxVersionTested is the newest version the app was tested against, which decides the behavior it gets

findings.own: a MinVersion or MaxVersionTested that is not four 16-bit numbers, and a MinVersion higher than the MaxVersionTested of the same TargetDeviceFamily, which says the app was never tested on a build it installs on

findings.fix: use a scheme of the app's own, such as contoso-notes; to open web links, let the default browser handle them

basis.text: Windows comes with handlers for schemes such as http, https, mailto, ms-settings and ms-store, and the user picks the app that opens a scheme

findings.found: the Language "en_IE" is not a well-formed BCP 47 tag: it holds a character other than letters, digits and hyphens; BCP 47 separates subtags with a hyphen

basis.text: the Language of a Resource is a BCP 47 language tag, and the first Resource names the default language

findings.own: a Resource Language that is not a well-formed BCP 47 tag: subtags of letters and digits separated by hyphens, in the order language, script, region, variants, extensions and private use; whether a subtag is in the IANA registry is not checked
